title: External Application Head-Requirement Binding and Decision-Margin Qualification

canonical_context.authority_note: Context only; F-GC08 is research and does not modify canonical production source.

frozen_application_class.scope: A groundwater-management or environmental-impact decision in which head or drawdown is compared with an externally governed threshold at specified locations and times.
frozen_application_class.reason_for_selection: This is the only F-GC06 class in which groundwater head or drawdown itself is the decision quantity, so an external decision requirement could in principle bind directly to H_app without crop-response or recharge-sensitivity propagation.

research_question: Can an independently governed decision threshold be accompanied by a traceable allowable predictive error or decision margin that can legitimately instantiate H_app and then be composed with F-GC07 temporal/coupling characterization?
candidate_source_classes: project approval or compliance documents with explicit head/drawdown triggers
independent uncertainty guidance for groundwater decision support
published groundwater impact assessments only when the provenance of their decision margin is traceable

acceptance_rule.required_for_numeric_H_app: An external source must state, or make mechanically derivable from an explicit governed decision rule, the acceptable prediction error or safety margin for the head/drawdown decision. The value must be independent of SWAP5, MODFLOW solver tolerance, F-GC02 target behavior and F-GC07 numerical results.
acceptance_rule.required_for_numeric_H_budget: A defensible temporal allocation must additionally be specified or derived from an independently governed total-error allocation rule. F-GC07 estimator ratios may characterize numerical behavior but may not choose the policy fraction.
acceptance_rule.fail_closed: If the source supplies only an impact/management threshold but no acceptable predictive error or decision margin, do not infer H_app from the threshold magnitude.

GC07_evidence_may_support: predictor-corrector correction as a same-window numerical signal
residual contraction as a numerical signal
cost and mass-conservation characterization within the tested domain
